## Conclusion
A high radial 1X component should not by itself be called rotor unbalance, because misalignment can also produce or change radial 1X components as well as 2X, 3X, and higher harmonics [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0032_00050].
Classify the case as more consistent with rotor unbalance when the dominant lateral vibration is synchronous 1X, locked to shaft rotation, tracks running speed during shutdown, and shows the usual rotor unbalance vector behavior such as a changed 1X vector after a balance change [bakerhughes_bn_fbd5b29e_p0005_00009] [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052].
Use speed/phase behavior as an additional rotor unbalance discriminator: rotor unbalance vibration is largest when speed coincides with a rotor critical speed, has a significant phase change through the critical speed, and is constant at fixed speed [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052].
Classify the case as more consistent with shaft misalignment when high radial 1X is accompanied by strong 2X or higher harmonic content, because shaft misalignment is listed with 1X, 2X, or higher-order harmonic frequencies [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052].
Look especially for axial vibration to separate misalignment from pure rotor unbalance: angular misalignment causes axial vibration as well as radial vibration, combined misalignment commonly includes axial vibration, and axial vibration is therefore a sign of misalignment [vold_kalman_e0e977fa_p0022_00029].
For precision diagnosis of misalignment, examine the FFT or power spectrum for 2X or 4X components rather than relying only on radial 1X [vold_kalman_e0e977fa_p0022_00030].
Other misalignment checks are load sensitivity and coupling-end axial phase: misalignment amplitude is relatively insensitive to speed but generally rises with load, and axial vibration on the two sides of the coupling is basically 180° out of phase [vold_kalman_e0e977fa_p0022_00030].
A practical rule is: high radial 1X with stable synchronous behavior and rotor unbalance-like speed/phase response points toward rotor unbalance, whereas high radial 1X plus axial vibration, 2X/4X or higher harmonics, load sensitivity, and 180° axial phase across the coupling points toward misalignment [bakerhughes_bn_fbd5b29e_p0005_00009] [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052] [vold_kalman_e0e977fa_p0022_00029] [vold_kalman_e0e977fa_p0022_00030].

s3.answer:
A high radial 1X component should not by itself be called unbalance, because misalignment can also produce or change radial 1X components as well as 2X, 3X, and higher harmonics [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0032_00050].
Classify the case as more consistent with unbalance when the dominant lateral vibration is synchronous 1X, locked to shaft rotation, tracks running speed during shutdown, and shows the usual unbalance vector behavior such as a changed 1X vector after a balance change [bakerhughes_bn_fbd5b29e_p0005_00009] [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052].
Use speed/phase behavior as an additional unbalance discriminator: unbalance vibration is largest when speed coincides with a rotor critical speed, has a significant phase change through the critical speed, and is constant at fixed speed [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052].
Classify the case as more consistent with shaft misalignment when high radial 1X is accompanied by strong 2X or higher harmonic content, because shaft misalignment is listed with 1X, 2X, or higher-order harmonic frequencies [gbt_19873_1_2005_1_57afcb1a_p0033_00052].
Look especially for axial vibration to separate misalignment from pure unbalance: angular misalignment causes axial vibration as well as radial vibration, combined misalignment commonly includes axial vibration, and axial vibration is therefore a sign of misalignment [vold_kalman_e0e977fa_p0022_00029].
